gate_1_artifact.status: PASS on both legs, and now with BOTH operands quantised: 38.73 dB / SSIM 0.9672 against a 28 dB / 0.92 bar
gate_1_artifact.targets: int8 bytes = 1.296 GiB +/- 1 MiB; PSNR >= 28 dB, SSIM >= 0.92 vs FP32 (host simulation)
gate_1_artifact.evidence: docs/device/RESULTS_gate1.md + artifacts/manifest.json. INT8 payload 1,391,984,640 B = delta 0 against the reference; 30 regions of 46,399,488 B (44.25 MiB, limit 47.29); 300/300 GEMMs cosine >= 0.999 (worst 0.999922, ffn.net.2); MAC-weighted rel. Frobenius 0.93% (worst 1.25%), better than the 3-5% expected; coverage 1317 tensors = 300 INT8 + 525 FP16 + 492 expert-deferred, 0 orphaned; byte identity re-derived by an independent verifier (61 s vs the quantiser's 40 s). FP16 remainder is 54,024,320 B of payload in 54,573,056 B of files (the balance is 4096-B alignment padding - manifest totals/fp16_bytes vs totals/fp16_file_bytes). || END-TO-END LEG (phase1_quant/psnr_gate1.py, commit 2e4654b): all 36 decoder layers rebuilt from the INT8 artifact against fp32 give 40.22 dB PSNR / SSIM 0.9708, against a bar of 28 dB / 0.92. 36/36 reconstructions reproduce the manifest rel_fro to 4.5e-07, so the rebuild is the artifact and not a lookalike. || BOTH-OPERAND LEG (docs/device/RESULTS_gate1_actquant.md, commit 4096d98): with real calibrated activation scales on BOTH operands, 38.73 dB / SSIM 0.9672 - a 10.73 dB margin. Weight-only was 40.22 / 0.9708, so quantising ALL activations costs 1.49 dB / 0.0036 SSIM.
gate_1_artifact.not_measured: frame-level PSNR/SSIM through the full 9-frame decode (this is a per-layer reconstruction leg, not a rendered-video leg); activation quantisation (SA) still absent, so the device path is unverified end to end
gate_1_artifact.attribution: The whole cost sits in TWO layers. Leaving decoder.up_blocks.0 and .1 upsamplers.0.time_conv (the pair that miss the 0.999 cosine bar under the locked scale scheme) in fp32 recovers 48.99 dB / SSIM 0.9962 - i.e. those two layers cost 8.77 dB and 0.0254 SSIM. IMPORTANT GENERAL LESSON: their MAC share is 41.51 of 5,149.68 GMAC = 0.81%, so a 0.81% MAC share buys 8.8 dB of damage. MAC share is a poor proxy for output sensitivity; quantisation error has to be attributed by MEASURED output effect, layer by layer. The earlier MAC-share note in gate_1_vae_int8 correctly hedged this, and the measurement landed on the pessimistic side of the hedge.
gate_1_artifact.recommended_fix: Exempt those two layers from INT8 rather than adopting the per-(channel,tap) scale fork: they are 0.81% of the decoder's MACs, and T_V is not the binding constraint (see p3_8b_T_V_is_not_the_lever), so running 41.5 GMAC in fp32 on another engine is close to free and buys 8.77 dB / 0.025 SSIM. That converts a known Gate-1 miss into a solved one without touching the locked scale scheme.
gate_1_artifact.margin_is_not_where_you_think: The mean has 10.73 dB of room but the margin is not uniform: f0 loses 9.47 dB, putting the first frame at roughly 29.3 dB - only ~1.3 dB above the bar. Frame 0 is the binding element and the place any future regression lands first. Mechanistically sensible for a causal temporal decode: frame 0 has no temporal prior, so it is the only frame with nothing to lean on. Any change to the quantisation scheme (per-timestep scales, the 1x1-CONV_2D switch) should be judged on f0, not on the mean.
gate_1_artifact.error_budget_contrast: The two operands are not equally fragile here, which inverts the usual expectation: quantising ALL activations costs 1.49 dB, while exempting the two time_conv weight layers was worth 8.77 dB. The weight-side exemptions dominate this model's error budget and the activation operand is the cheap one. Practical consequence: exempt those two layers, wire real SA, and essentially all recoverable accuracy is recovered.

gate_4_parity.status: FAILS on device, and the failure is structural: only 25.8% of each [384,1536] TPU output tile is bit-exact against an exact host reference
gate_4_parity.targets: per-block cosine >= 0.999 vs FP32; frame PSNR >= 28 dB, SSIM >= 0.92
gate_4_parity.evidence: docs/device/RESULTS_gate3_parity.md + tools/pipe/gate3_parity.py (commit b5f26c2). Host reference is exact by construction: fp32 BLAS with K-split partials < 2^24, accumulated int64, requantised clamp(round(acc/127)), validated against brute-force int64 including the all -128 worst case. GEMM-level cosine from RESULTS_scales.md (40/40 per-column pass) still stands for the WEIGHTS; this is the DEVICE OUTPUT that fails.
gate_4_parity.failure_structure: LOCALIZED to the M (row) direction by P3.7b (docs/device/RESULTS_gate3_bisect.md, commit 95c8404, 32 graphs / 5 captures, basis activations A[r][r%K]=127 so the expected element is one stored weight byte - no saturation, no rounding ambiguity). 100.00% bit-exact: M=1 x N=1536; M in {8,128,160,192,200} x N=384; M=128 x N in {128,768}. Partial: N=1536 at M=256/320/384 = 50.67/50.60/25.83% (the M=384 control reproduces Gate 3 to two decimals: 25.828% both runs). The M=384 'last column block exact' signature is M=384-specific; at M=256/320 all four column blocks are equal at ~50.7%, and the first row is always 100%.
gate_4_parity.compile_vs_exact_coincidence: For N <= 768, compile-success and exactness are the SAME boundary: N=384 is exact at M<=200 and refuses to compile at M>=208; N=768 is exact at M=128 and refuses at M=192. Only the wide N=1536 graphs compile everywhere (M=1..384) and they are exact only at M=1. That reads as ONE internal resource limit with two symptoms - reject below the limit, and internal-split-with-broken-writeback above it - rather than an arbitrary hole. The compile failures are non-monotonic in shape (384x1536 compiles while 384x384 and 192x768 do not), which fits a size-dependent split heuristic.
gate_4_parity.output_byte_hypothesis: Expressed in output bytes the boundary is nearly monotone: exact at <=147,456 B (M=192,N=768) and at 76,800 B (M=200,N=384); partial at 393,216 B (M=256,N=1536), 491,520 B (M=320) and 589,824 B (M=384) and 1,720,320 B (M=192,N=8960 = 14.2%). So the cap lies in [147,456 B, 393,216 B]. This is a hypothesis with a cheap test: two graphs at the SAME output-byte count in different shapes - M=256,N=768 and M=128,N=1536, both 196,608 B. Exact => cap above 196 kB and the recipe can be cut; partial => the cap is at or below it.
gate_4_parity.execute_count_is_the_cost: The recipe's dispatch count is set by the cap, not by taste: graphs per 1536-wide GEMM = (1530 x 1536)/cap, so under a 147 kB cap the floor is ~143 executes/block, at ~200 kB it is ~106, at 393 kB ~54 (today: 36). Their N in {128,384,768} x M<=200 recipe gives 112 - consistent with a ~190-200 kB cap, i.e. already near-optimal IF that is the cap. Nailing the cap therefore decides whether P3.7c will measure 54, 112 or 143 dispatches per block, a 2.6x spread in the dominant cost term.
gate_4_parity.open_discriminator: The 4x-compute worry is largely retired: every block that lands is 100.00% exact on basis activations, so the FC arithmetic per block is right and the loss is output that is missing or stale, not miscalculated - T_N is probably NOT 4x optimistic. The live risk has changed shape: the exact recipe needs ~112 executes/block against 36 today, and the TPU already runs at 5.6% of peak, so dispatch overhead may dominate. The indicative 1.18-2.01 ms/graph (2 executes, ungated) implies 132-225 ms/block - BELOW today's 377.8 ms - but those figures are not usable. P3.7c's gated, repeated-execute measurement is the number that decides whether an exact NPU stage is worth having at all.

gate_1_vae_int8.measured: 36 decoder layers, 100 taps, 592 CONV_2D executes/chunk - independently equal to the plan's count (configs/vae/plan_npu.json), so the INT8 builder and vae_export.py agree on the op walk. 72,685,152 B INT8 unpadded = layers.json exactly, 72,751,648 B with 4096-B tap windows (+0.091%); 42,636 B per-output-channel scales and 42,636 B of FP32 biases = the SAME 10,659 channels, an internal consistency check that passes. Verifier: 100/100 taps byte-identical to a from-source re-quantisation. Layout proof by end-to-end activation (not weight cosine): random activation through checkpoint weight vs dequantised INT8 taps under the same 2-D SAME conv gives 0.93/1.47/1.40% relFro and cosine 0.99996/0.99989/0.99990. Commit 8afaf61, docs/device/RESULTS_vae_int8.md.
gate_1_vae_int8.scale_scheme_fork: Under the locked per-output-column scheme, decoder.up_blocks.0.upsamplers.0.time_conv (cosine 0.997397) and decoder.up_blocks.1.upsamplers.0.time_conv (0.997484) FAIL the Gate-1 bar of 0.999 - 2 of 36. Per-(channel,tap) scales reach 0.999910 worst-in-decoder and pass. The artifact keeps the locked scheme; the fork is measured and NOT adopted, which is correct procedure - but it means the shippable decode carries a known Gate-1 miss.
gate_1_vae_int8.is_the_miss_cosmetic: MAC share of the two failing layers is 0.11% + 0.70% = 0.81% of the decoder's 5149.68 GMAC (5.41 + 36.10 GMAC), so their DIRECT numerical impact is small. That bound does NOT cover propagation: both are temporal upsamplers early in the decode (up_blocks.0 and .1 of 3), so their error is re-amplified by everything downstream. MAC share therefore says 'do not panic', not 'do not care' - the end-to-end PSNR/SSIM leg is the only thing that settles it and it is unrun.
gate_1_vae_int8.reporting_trap: The verifier's 'mean relFro 2.000%' is an UNWEIGHTED mean over 100 taps; Gate-1's 0.93% is MAC-weighted. They are not comparable and should never appear side by side unlabelled - the weighted figure is the one that predicts output error.
gate_1_vae_int8.blocked_on_SA: Bias stays FP32 because an INT32 bias needs SA (the input activation scale) and calibrate.py does not exist. No scale invented - correct. NOTE that the FP32 forward pass is the single artifact that unblocks THREE things at once: the Gate-1 PSNR/SSIM reference, SA for the INT32 bias, and the activation quantisation for convseq. .venv-ref already supplies torch 2.15.0+cpu / diffusers 0.43.0 / transformers 5.23.0, so this is code-only work and it is arguably more on the critical path than the convseq run itself. convseq's FIRST question (does this HAL accept TENSOR_QUANT8_SYMM_PER_CHANNEL on CONV_2D) does not need SA and is worth keeping first as a cheap compile/support probe.

phase3_pipeline.p3_2_open_decision: ONE INT8 COPY vs GPU SPEED. The project premise is a single copy shared by both engines; zero-copy import costs 32% of the GPU stage, and staging to device-local memory recovers it only by making a second copy. Both branches are measured (25.55 s vs 31.75 s period), so this is now the student's call. UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS worth one experiment first: on a unified-memory SoC the Mali GPU and the CPU share the same LPDDR4X, so a 32% per-byte penalty is more consistent with a cache-attribute/mapping effect in clImportMemoryARM (uncached or write-through mapping) than with bandwidth physics - the working-set scaling fits that reading. Route A (AHardwareBuffer, which Gate 2 verified also imports) and/or different import hints are the cheap tests; if either recovers the 32%, the one-copy premise survives at full speed.

phase3_pipeline.p3_4_launch_order_is_correctness: Both binaries reset_headers() when they map the ring, so a consumer that maps late WIPES a producer's publish and the run dies 300 s later as chunk_never_published. The runner now waits for the consumer's READY before starting the producer. That is a correctness dependency, not a convenience: a refactor that reorders the launch reintroduces a failure that presents as a hang. It deserves a test that fails on the wrong order, because nothing else in the harness would catch it.

phase3_pipeline.p3_5_GPU_DERATES: THE GPU DOES NOT HOLD ITS RATE. The Mali block goes 203.0 -> 274.2 ms/block (+35.1%) starting at block ~1135 (~230 s of continuous GPU work): a STEP with no recovery, and it clears with cooldown, so it is thermal state, not wear. The NPU stays flat (396.5 -> 394.0 ms). A post-stream one-closure pass measured 251.2 ms against 166.2 ms cold, so the derate is engine-wide, not closure-specific. Every cold-start T_G in this lock is therefore a COLD-START number: the sustained period is 43.87 s at k_b=160, or 37.85 s at the re-solved k_b=138 (T_G 0.2742). Reported, locks on rates untouched.

Additive is closer (+71 ms for 10 closures vs +85 ms for one) but not exact. A compute-clock throttle scales multiplicatively; a bandwidth / weight-streaming cap hits the more compute-efficient form harder - which is the shape observed. That points at the memory path, the same place the unresolved 'import penalty' lives, so the two anomalies may be one phenomenon. Test on the next run, not by argument.

phase3_pipeline.p3_16_CORRECTION_GATE1_IS_END_TO_END: CORRECTING MY OWN P3.16 NOTE. I claimed Gate 1's 38.73 dB was a PER-LAYER reconstruction and therefore not comparable to the decode's 20.59 dB, and that the 18 dB was 'accumulation, not a defect'. THAT IS WRONG. phase1_quant/psnr_gate1.py:197,268 line 283 runs `b = vae.decode(z).sample` and scores frame-level PSNR over the full 9-frame output - it is END-TO-END, exactly like the device. Its only per-layer content is the weight round-trip relFro check. So 38.73 dB (both operands INT8, real torch ops) and 20.59 dB (vae_sim, device semantics) are the SAME kind of measurement over the SAME latent, and the 18.14 dB between them is the cost of the DEVICE'S EXECUTION DECOMPOSITION - per-tap int8 rounding, INT32 bias, per-tap requant, tap gather order - not accumulation and not precision. That is a defect to find, not a law of the universe.
phase3_pipeline.p3_16_the_gap_that_must_be_localised: Restated with the correction: the same quantised tensors give 38.73 dB through torch ops and 20.59 dB through vae_sim's device semantics, while vae_sim tracks the real device to 0.15 dB. So the 18.14 dB lives in the semantics the device imposes, and the HAL is exonerated (98.59% bit-identical per conv). The per-layer oracle arm is therefore the PRIMARY instrument now, not a secondary one: feeding each conv the reference's own input shows whether the decomposition (bias/requant/rounding per tap) loses fidelity at each layer or only in aggregate.
phase3_pipeline.p3_16_activation_operand_already_measure: Retracting the 'missing cell' too - it is not missing. Both Gate-1 legs are end-to-end: int8 weights with fp32 activations 40.22 dB, both operands INT8 38.73 dB. So the activation operand costs 1.49 dB END TO END, not per layer, and 8-bit activations are NOT the reason the device sits at 20.59. The precision-limit hypothesis is dead before it cost a run.
phase3_pipeline.p3_16_where_that_leaves_the_hunt: Attributable budget for the 18.14 dB, in the order the measurements support: (1) per-tap INT32 bias - measured as a real per-layer effect (bias-once moved layers 0-29 by +0.0099 cosine) but currently MASKED by the layer-34 defect, worth -0.29 dB net until layer 34 is fixed; (2) per-tap requant - +0.04 dB, i.e. free, so it is not the cause; (3) per-tap int8 ROUNDING of the activations at each tap - UNMEASURED, and the most likely residue given (1) and (2) are small; (4) the tap gather - already fixed once, worth 8.84 dB, so a second similar error cannot be excluded. Recommendation: run the oracle arm (it separates (1)/(3) from (4) in one pass), then price per-tap rounding explicitly.

Chunk to <=1664, one compilation per op (ffn.down = 7x FC[1536,1280] + 6x ADD, 2.57 s total); chunking inside a single graph does NOT work (down2 = 2x K=4480 + ADD, all ops supported, compile OP_FAILED at 47.8 s).
npu_constraints.graph_shape: one graph per (block, token-tile); whole-block graphs validated and were SUPPORTED by google-edgetpu but Compilation_finish REBOOTED THE DEVICE (2026-11-15) -> one graph per GEMM is the only viable path
npu_constraints.weight_scales: per-tensor only: TENSOR_QUANT8_SYMM_PER_CHANNEL is rejected by FULLY_CONNECTED with addOperation BAD_DATA(4), so the per-output-column scheme cannot be expressed on the NPU stage. DECISION PENDING, but no longer a guess - the cost is measured on the real checkpoint (docs/device/RESULTS_scales.md, 40 GEMM instances = blocks 0/5/15/29 x 10): per-tensor costs 2.15x the mean GEMM output error (3.01% vs 1.40%; median-of-ratios 1.74x, worst 5.44x) and breaks the Gate-1 cosine>=0.999 bar on 6/40 outputs (worst 0.996820), where per-column breaks 0/40 (min 0.999926). The penalty is a WEIGHT property, not a shape property: it tracks per-column scale spread at r=0.805 (per-column error vs spread r=0.101), so a shape-based restriction is unsupportable; the only defensible restriction is per-tensor-where-cheap, attn2.to_k + attn2.to_v = 10.2% of block MACs, leaving 89.8% of block MACs unable to use the NPU under the locked quantisation.
